article.name: Honcho
article.summary: Honcho is a memory service and library for stateful agents. It stores peer-attributed messages in sessions, processes them asynchronously into conclusions and representations, and exposes semantic search, context and chat APIs. Workspaces, tenants and named scopes define important data boundaries; runtime benchmark behavior was not measured.

who_what.text: The repository is maintained under the Plastic Labs GitHub organization. Its README describes this repository as the core FastAPI service and identifies managed, local-stack and self-hosted use modes; no individual maintainer is asserted here.
The catalog identifies ordinal 308 as Honcho, slug honcho, with an explicit listed repository URL. Its Atlas attribution is retained only for roster context, not assessment evidence.

architecture.text: The data model centers on workspaces, peers, sessions and messages. Messages are peer-attributed and ordered within sessions; peer conclusions and representations summarize information across sessions, while named scopes constrain which sessions contribute to reads.

The write path stores messages in PostgreSQL and enqueues reasoning work; deriver workers asynchronously generate conclusions and representations. The repository also supplies search, vector-store, SDK, CLI and agent integration components.

Conclusions are documents tied to observer/observed perspectives. Source-conclusion and source-message links preserve derivation references; the graph API can expose those links and whether lineage is complete or unresolved.

behavior.text: The documented write flow creates peers and sessions and appends messages; the API also supports explicit conclusion creation. Current architecture documentation describes storage and queue insertion in the request, with LLM derivation outside the synchronous write path.

Message update operations and conclusion deletion are exposed. The conclusion delete route describes the action as irreversible and removes copied Representation History; this review did not verify physical erasure from every backing store, backup or external copy.

Retrieval includes peer/workspace chat, session context, representations, semantic conclusion queries, message search and an experimental Arrow graph endpoint. Conclusion queries require an observer/observed pair; message search supports semantic/text retrieval with context and session-scope controls.

Workspaces and tenant row-level security separate applications/tenants. Named scopes are reserved peers representing session groups; scope reads bind to the caller's authorized scope key, and peer-scoped keys cannot request named-scope reads.

Source conclusion and message IDs can be retained on derived documents. The graph export marks complete, partial, unknown and not-applicable lineage and counts unresolved source categories; links do not independently prove the derived claim.

Source-visible efficiency and observability include asynchronous derivation, bounded search and graph work, queue/status surfaces, stage timing, graph counters, ETags and Prometheus instrumentation. These are implementation observations, not benchmark measurements.

metrics.evidence: Search, chat and representation APIs exist; no answerable or unanswerable fixture questions were run.
Message updates, asynchronous derivation and conclusion lifecycle APIs exist; no correction history or stale-value probes were scored.
Conclusion and other deletion paths are documented, but no post-delete recall probes or storage audit were run.
Workspace, tenant, peer and named-scope boundaries are implemented; no cross-scope or cross-tenant probes were run.

limits.text: This is a bounded inspection of official repository documentation and selected current source at one verified commit. Honcho, its tests and benchmarks were not run; source inspection cannot establish runtime answer quality, deployment isolation, deletion completeness or queue behavior.

The project supports different managed, self-hosted and local configurations, optional multi-tenant mode, external vector backends and model providers. Correctness of a particular deployment's database roles, row-level security and provider settings was not tested.

The review did not establish physical deletion across backups, vector indexes and external copies, nor that every natural-language answer exposes source citations. Those outcomes require deployment-specific inspection and adjudicated runtime probes.
